# EDA findings (generated by 03_eda.ipynb)

1. A no-buffer dealer quoting the latest premium and buying 2 rounds later was underwater on 64% of Cat A and 64% of Cat B sales since 2023, losing S$4,920 (A) and S$6,180 (B) per underwater car on average; the worst 2-round rise was S$20,216.
2. Premiums rose from S$19,190 (Cat B, Jan 2010) to S$131,901 (Oct 2026), 6.9x; Cat A from S$18,502 to S$132,004 (7.1x). This is why we model the % rise, not the S$ rise.
3. In % terms the 2-round rise is narrower today than in 2010-14 (90th percentile +15.5% -> +9.0%, std. dev. 13.5% -> 7.4%), but because premiums are far higher its 90th percentile in S$ moved from S$8,631 to S$9,161: the dollar risk has not fallen even though % swings have. Skewness by period: 2010-14 +1.79, 2015-19 +0.25, 2020-22 +0.36, 2023-26 -0.94.
4. The 2-round rise in Cat B exceeded 10% in 8% of rounds since 2023 (7 of 90).
5. Volatility clusters: the 12-round volatility of Cat B ranged from 3.6% (10th pct) to 11.4% (90th pct), and the lag-1 autocorrelation of absolute 1-round changes is 0.33 for Cat B, so calm and turbulent spells persist. Buffers should widen with recent volatility.
6. Demand pressure is only a weak signal on its own: in Cat B the mean 2-round rise is +1.7% in the lowest octile of the bid ratio and +1.1% in the highest (correlation -0.00).
7. Supply moves price in levels: log quota and log premium correlate at -0.28 (A), -0.48 (B), -0.81 (E). The 2013 low-quota years coincide with S$70k-90k premiums; the 2017-20 high-quota years with S$30k-50k.
8. Little linear momentum: the lag-1 autocorrelation of 1-round changes is -0.13 (A), -0.01 (B), +0.32 (E). Momentum features should add little to point forecasts; the value is in the spread (volatility), not the direction.
9. The log premium is non-stationary (ADF p = 0.12-0.76) while its changes are stationary (p < 0.001), so Phase 5 models changes (rises), not levels.
10. For Cat B since 2023, the 90th percentile of the 2-round rise is S$10,036 and the 95th S$12,220 (plan's preliminary check: S$9,977 and S$11,889).
